Meta Ventures Into Robotics with 'Max' Humanoid Prototype Developed Alongside Chinese Startup

Key takeaways Meta's First Humanoid Robot Prototype Social media and technology giant Meta has entered the robotics sector by developing a humanoid robot prototype named "Max." According to published reports, the project was created in collaboration with Fourier, a Chinese robotics

Meta's First Humanoid Robot Prototype

Social media and technology giant Meta has entered the robotics sector by developing a humanoid robot prototype named "Max." According to published reports, the project was created in collaboration with Fourier, a Chinese robotics startup, through a joint effort that spanned roughly three months.

The prototype stands about 1.5 meters (approximately five feet) tall and weighs around 48 kilograms (106 pounds). It is powered by Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip. Reports indicate that Meta's robotics team collaborated on-site in China, with Vice President of Robotics Products Li-Chen Miller spending about two months at Fourier's Shanghai factory.

Reported Features and Capabilities

Published reports outline several intended features for the Max prototype, designed to serve as a physical embodiment of Meta's "Muse" AI agent:

  • Facial Expression Display: Equipped with a built-in display intended to mimic facial expressions and built-in speakers.
  • Dexterous Hands: Features five-fingered hands engineered to grasp and handle small objects.
  • Domestic Assistance Goals: Designed with the long-term objective of potentially aiding with everyday household chores.

Additionally, reports note that Meta initiated work on a successor version, designated Max 2, in September. Proposed updates for this next iteration include a redesigned torso, improved hands, an integrated projector, and extra sensors to assist with navigating stairs.

Research Status and Market Availability

Confirmed information indicates that Max remains strictly an internal research prototype. Meta has stated that its work with Fourier is limited to internal experimentation and research, with no current plans to commercialize or sell the robot to the general public.

Because the hardware and underlying software—including technologies from recent acquisitions like the AI startup Assured Robot Intelligence (ARI)—are still in the developmental and experimental phase, there is no official timeline for when or if a consumer-ready version will become available.

Practical Implications and Verification

  • Consumer Expectations: Consumers should note that Max is not a commercially available product.
  • Verification: Users interested in official developments can monitor Meta's official corporate announcements and engineering blog posts for verified updates on its hardware and artificial intelligence research.

*Disclaimer: Claims regarding the prototype's specifications and development timeline are based on reported accounts and internal company disclosures rather than final commercial specifications.*
